chunks: And narrated to me 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim and Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, all from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from 'Ali ibn Fadhl from Abi Jamilah from Jabir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The heavens never wept over anyone after Yahya ibn Zakariyya (peace be upon him) except over al-Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him). Indeed, they wept over him for forty days.

key_terms.أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْماً: For forty days, indicating the duration of the celestial weeping
key_terms.السَّمَاءُ: The heavens/sky, representing the celestial realm
key_terms.يَحْيَى بْنُ زَكَرِيَّا: Yahya ibn Zakariyya (John the son of Zechariah), a prophet

ai.seo_question: Who did the heavens weep for after Yahya ibn Zakariyya?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) to emphasize the cosmic scale of Imam al-Husayn’s martyrdom, noting that the heavens wept for forty days—a duration often associated with the period of mourning and the opening of the gates of heaven. This unique honor, shared only with Yahya ibn Zakariyya (a.s.), underscores the Ahl al-Bayt’s role as the focal points of divine mercy and the natural world’s response to their suffering. The narration serves as a theological affirmation of the Imam’s status, linking earthly tragedy with celestial grief.
